name: data_edit
description: A data source's rows (SPEC §3.10). With no `edits`, the source as a sheet: its columns, each one's type, its rows as written, by index from 0, and the cells a column does not read. With them, cells set (`set`), rows added (`add`, at `row` or the end) and taken away (`remove`), in order, all or none: one write of the source's file that keeps every other byte, or a patch of rows written inline, and what that changes in what lint finds. A value its column's type refuses stops them, by index (`op`); edits that would leave the deck invalid are refused (`refused`, and why in `added`). Every chart and table that reads the source reads it changed.

RowEdit.description: An edit of a data source's rows. Row 0 is the first after the header.

oneOf.description:
`column` of row `row`, set to `value` as typed: a number, `true` or `false`, a date as the
column's `parse` format or ISO 8601 reads it, or any text. Empty, or null, is nothing.

A row added at `row`, the rows from there on after it; at the end without it. Each column
is its value in `values`, as typed, or nothing.

bundle.description: The bundle: a directory, a `.scaena` zip, or a `deck.json`.

source.description: The source's id: what a chart or a table names as `@id`.

edits.description:
The edits, made in order, all or none: each names a row as the edits before it leave the
rows. With none, the source is read, and nothing is written.

dry_run.description: Say what would change, and write nothing.

Sheet.description:
A source as an editor shows it: its columns, each one's type, and each row's cells as
written. Edits name a row by its place here, from 0, and a column by its name.

rows.description:
Each row's cells, in the columns' order: a value as the source writes it, text without its
quotes, and nothing as empty.

problems.description:
Each cell its column does not read, and why: what a chart that reads the source refuses
(E103), until an edit sets the cell to what it reads.

type.description:
How the source's `schema` types it (`string` where it says nothing): what a value set in
it must read as.

ColumnType.description: What a column holds, from the source's `schema` (`string` when it says nothing).

CellProblem.description: A cell of a sheet that its column's type does not read.

Finding.description: One lint finding, shaped for agents: a code, a JSON pointer, and (when safe) a fix.

file.description: The bundle file `path` points into, when it is not `deck.json` (a theme file).

format.description: The format the deck was laid out in (`"9:16"`), when it is not the deck's own.

fix.description: A JSON Patch (RFC 6902) that resolves the finding. Only safe, non-content fixes.

edited.description: Whether it was written: not under a dry run, with no edits, nor when refused.

file.description: The file it is, which an edit writes; none for rows written inline, which are the deck's.

sheet.description:
The source as it reads after the edits, or as it is where there are none or they are
refused: its columns, their types, its rows as written, and the cells a column does not
read.

added.description: What `validate` and `lint` find after the edits that they did not before.

removed.description: What they found before that they do not after.

errors.description: The findings that are errors, after.

refused.description: Refused: the edits would have added a validation finding (in `added`).
